questions.scenario: During the excavation and construction of a cast-in-place reinforced concrete cantilever retaining wall, the RGBC's site team encounters unexpected groundwater ingress. The RGBC Authorized Signatory (AS) unilaterally decides to insert weep holes and structural shear dowels differing substantially from the approved plans, without notifying the Authorized Person (AP) or the Building Authority (BA). Under Section 9(5)(b) and Section 40(2A) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), what is the statutory duty and legal exposure of the RGBC?
options: A. The RGBC has no duty to notify the BA directly because design alterations are solely the professional responsibility of the AP and RSE.

B. The RGBC must give immediate written notice to the BA upon discovering any divergence or defect; carrying out works resulting in material divergence without prior approval is an offence under Section 40(2A).
C. The RGBC is permitted to diverge from approved plans under site emergency provisions provided retrospective approval is submitted within 28 days of completing the retaining wall.
D. The RGBC is only required to record the divergence in the site logbook and have the RSE countersign the as-built drawings upon application for temporary occupation permit.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 9(5)(b), an RGBC must give written notice to the Building Authority if it is found that the building works diverge materially from the approved plans or if any defect occurs. Carrying out works materially diverging from approved plans without approval constitutes a strict criminal offence under Section 40(2A)(b). There is no statutory emergency defense allowing unilateral alterations without notice or retrospective plan approval within 28 days.

questions.scenario: When granting consent under Section 16(1)(b) for deep rock-socketed steel H-pile foundation works, the Building Authority imposes a statutory condition under Section 17(1)(a) requiring proof drilling down to 5 metres below the pile toe level for every socket. The RGBC AS determines that drilling 3 metres is geotechnically adequate and instructs the piling team to omit the remaining 2 metres to avoid delay. What are the statutory consequences under the Buildings Ordinance?
options: A. The RGBC can vary the drilling depth upon agreement in writing by the Registered Geotechnical Engineer (RGE) without seeking the BA's consent.
B. Failure to comply with a condition imposed by the BA under Section 17(1)(a) is a criminal offence under Section 40(2AA), punishable by fine and imprisonment.
C. The condition under Section 17(1)(a) is merely advisory and cannot be enforced unless a ground collapse or settlement occurs.
D. The BA may only issue a non-statutory advisory letter and cannot refer the matter for criminal prosecution under Cap. 123.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 17(1)(a), the Building Authority has the power to attach conditions to consents, including proof drilling or testing. Under Section 40(2AA), any person who fails to comply with a condition imposed under Section 17(1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 6 and imprisonment for 2 years. Technical agreement with an RSE/RGE does not override a statutory condition imposed by the BA.

questions.scenario: An RGBC obtained consent under Section 16(1)(b) to commence superstructure works for a multi-storey development on 15 March. On 10 April, site operations were totally shut down due to a contractual dispute between the main contractor and client, and no further works occurred on site. It is now 20 July. What is the legal status of the consent under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123)?
options: A. The consent remains fully valid for 12 months from the date of issue under Regulation 27 of the Building (Administration) Regulations.

B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) because the works, having commenced, were suspended for a period exceeding 3 months; a renewal application via Form BA9 is required before resuming works.
C. The consent can be automatically revived by serving a 7-day resumption notice on Form BA10 to the Building Authority.
D. The consent is suspended but does not revoke until the Building Authority issues a formal gazette notice under Section 20(2).
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 20(1), a consent is deemed to be revoked if the building works are not commenced within 3 months of consent issuance, or if commenced, are suspended for a period exceeding 3 months. From 10 April to 20 July is over 3 months of suspension; therefore, the consent is revoked by operation of law. To resume, an application for renewal of consent under BO Section 20(2) and B(A)R Reg. 34 must be submitted on Form BA9. Note that B(A)R Regulation 27 has been repealed.

questions.scenario: Upon completion of a 30-storey commercial office building, the AP and RGBC submit Form BA13 and Form BA14 applying for an Occupation Permit (OP) under Section 21. During the final inspection, the Building Authority discovers that the designated refuge floor has been subdivided by lightweight partitions to house building service maintenance workshops, diverging from the approved architectural plans. Under Section 21(6), what statutory action will the Building Authority take?
options: A. The BA must issue a temporary occupation permit under Section 21(2) allowing occupancy while requiring the partitions to be removed within 6 months.
B. The BA must refuse to issue an occupation permit under Section 21(6)(d) because the building has not been completed in accordance with the approved plans in a material respect.
C. The BA can only refuse the OP under Section 21(6) if the unauthorized work causes immediate structural collapse of the refuge floor.
D. The BA must issue the OP unconditionally and subsequently issue a removal order under Section 24.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 21(6)(d), the Building Authority shall refuse to issue a temporary occupation permit or an occupation permit if the building has not been completed in accordance with the approved plans in any material respect. Refuge floor integrity is a vital life-safety requirement under the code and approved plans. The BA does not have the discretion to issue an OP or temporary OP in the presence of such material divergences.

questions.scenario: During ongoing deep excavation works for a 3-level basement adjoining an existing railway reserve, real-time settlement monitoring shows that adjacent ground movement has exceeded the statutory trigger limit of 20mm, reaching 35mm. The Building Authority serves a Cease Works Order under Section 23(1) of the Buildings Ordinance. If the RGBC continues excavation without the BA's written permission, what is the criminal liability?
options: A. The RGBC faces a civil penalty from MTR Corporation, but no criminal penalty under Cap. 123 until structural cracks appear.

B. Under Section 40(2C), any person who fails to comply with an order under Section 23(1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of $250,000 and 1 year imprisonment, plus daily fines.
C. The RGBC is only subject to Section 13 disciplinary proceedings and cannot be prosecuted in a criminal court.
D. The order is automatically stayed if the RGBC lodges an appeal to the Building Appeal Tribunal within 21 days.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 23(1), where building works are being carried out in such manner as to cause or be likely to cause risk of injury to persons or damage to property, the BA may order the cessation of works. Failure to comply with an order made under Section 23(1) is a criminal offence under Section 40(2C), liable to a fine of $250,000 and imprisonment for 1 year, alongside daily fines of $50,000. An appeal to the Appeal Tribunal does not automatically suspend the operation of a Section 23 emergency cease works order.

questions.scenario: A contractor on site executes unauthorized steel frame mezzanine platforms inside an industrial unit without approved plans or consent. The Building Authority serves an order under Section 24(1) requiring demolition and reinstatement. The owner and RGBC ignore the order. The BA proceeds to carry out the works using government contractors under Section 24(2). How are the costs recovered and what is the legal impact on the property?
options: A. The costs are absorbed by the BD enforcement budget, and the RGBC is fined an administrative fee of $5,000.
B. The expenses incurred by the BA, together with a surcharge, are recoverable from the owner and can be registered in the Land Registry as a statutory charge running with the land.
C. The BA must file a civil debt recovery claim in the District Court before it can demand reimbursement from the owner.
D. The BA can only recover expenses by seizing and auctioning the RGBC's construction equipment.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 24(2), where an order under Section 24(1) is not complied with, the Building Authority may demolish or alter the building works. Under Section 33, any expenses incurred by the BA (plus a supervision surcharge of up to 20%) are recoverable from the owner and may be registered in the Land Registry, creating a first legal charge on the property until fully paid.

questions.scenario: Due to improper deep excavation and lateral support (ELS) sequence carried out by an RGBC, severe ground subsidence occurs, causing significant structural cracking in an adjacent 6-storey pre-war tenement building. The Building Authority inspects the building and determines it is in a dangerous condition. Under Section 24A, what emergency statutory power may the Building Authority exercise?
options: A. The BA may apply to the District Court for a 14-day warrant to seize the RGBC's bank accounts.
B. The BA may make a Closure Order under Section 24A to prohibit entry or occupation of the dangerous building, requiring police assistance if necessary to evict occupants.
C. The BA must give 2 months' prior written notice to all tenants before any order to close the premises can be executed.
D. The BA can only direct the RGBC to pay temporary rental subsidies to the affected tenants without closing the building.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 24A, where the Building Authority is of the opinion that any building is in a dangerous condition or is likely to become dangerous, the BA may apply to a magistrate or make a Closure Order to close the building and prohibit entry by any person except authorized officers. This emergency public safety measure does not require 2 months' notice.

questions.scenario: To expedite the certification of structural completion on Form BA14, the RGBC Authorized Signatory knowingly submits mill test certificates for Grade B500B rebar that were fabricated from another project site, falsely declaring that the rebar used in the high-stress basement columns complied with the approved specification. Under Section 40(1AA) of the Buildings Ordinance, what criminal liability does the AS/RGBC face?
options: A. It is treated as an administrative discrepancy resolvable by paying a nominal re-testing surcharge to BD.
B. Any person who knowingly makes a false representation in any document submitted to the BA commits an offence liable on conviction to a fine of $1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years.
C. Criminal liability is strictly restricted to the Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) who countersigned the form.
D. The AS is liable only to disciplinary proceedings under Section 13, without any criminal jurisdiction by the courts.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 40(1AA), any person who knowingly makes any false declaration, or who knowingly gives any false certificate or representation in any form, certificate, notice, or document submitted to the Building Authority under the Buildings Ordinance, commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of $1,000,000 and to imprisonment for 3 years. This applies directly to the RGBC and AS.

questions.scenario: During the erection of external system formwork on a 45-storey residential tower, the RGBC skips every second tie-bolt anchor to speed up turnaround cycles. During high winds, the system formwork detaches, plummeting to the busy street below, destroying several vehicles and injuring two pedestrians. Under Section 40(2B)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance, what constitutes the statutory offense?
options: A. It is strictly an industrial accident under the Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance (Cap. 59), exempt from the Buildings Ordinance.
B. Carrying out building works in a manner likely to cause a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property is an offence punishable by a fine of $1,000,000 and 3 years imprisonment.
C. The RGBC is completely absolved if the site safety officer was absent from the site on certified sick leave.
D. Criminal liability under Section 40(2B) only arises if a total collapse of the permanent structure occurs.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 40(2B)(b), any person directly concerned with the carrying out of any building works or street works who carries out such works in a manner that causes or is likely to cause a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property commits an offence and is liable to a fine of $1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years. This covers temporary works and erection methods directly.

questions.scenario: Following an RGBC's conviction in court under Section 40(2A) for carrying out major unauthorized alteration works, the Building Authority refers the contractor to a Disciplinary Board under Section 13 of the Buildings Ordinance. What statutory sanctions can the Disciplinary Board order against the RGBC under Section 13(4)?
options: A. Impose a prison sentence of up to 2 years on the Authorized Signatory and order the forfeiture of the company's construction equipment.

B. Order that the contractor be removed from the register permanently or for a period, or be fined a maximum amount, and pay the costs of the inquiry, but it has no jurisdiction to impose custodial imprisonment.
C. Direct the Buildings Department to revoke the contractor's business registration certificate and close all active sites across Hong Kong.
D. Order mandatory retraining of site staff without the power to impose fines or suspend registration.
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 13(4), a Disciplinary Board has quasi-judicial powers to order the removal of the contractor/AS from the register (permanently or for a specified term), reprimand the person, impose a fine (up to $250,000 for registered contractors), and order payment of inquiry costs. Crucially, a Disciplinary Board is an administrative tribunal and does not possess criminal jurisdiction to impose custodial sentences (imprisonment) or revoke general business registration.

questions.scenario: A property developer removes the incumbent main contractor due to protracted delays on an ongoing residential superstructure project and decides to appoint a new Registered General Building Contractor (RGBC) to take over the site. Before the new RGBC can legitimately take possession and execute the building works, specific statutory notifications must be lodged with the Building Authority regarding the change in contractor.
options: A. The new RGBC must submit Form BA10 to the Building Authority within 48 hours of entering the site, signed solely by the new contractor's Authorized Signatory.

B. The person for whom the building works are being carried out must, within 7 days of the appointment, give notice to the Building Authority on specified Form BA8, accompanied by an acceptance of appointment signed by the new RGBC.
C. The Authorized Person (AP) must submit Form BA14 to cancel the previous contractor's registration on site and apply for a new consent before Form BA8 can be accepted.
D. The new RGBC may proceed under the existing contractor's consent immediately, provided Form BA8 is submitted within 28 days following the handover of site possession.
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1), every person for whom building works or street works are to be carried out must, within 7 days of appointing a Registered Contractor, give notice in writing to the Building Authority on specified Form BA8. Regulation 8(2) specifies that such notice must be accompanied by an acceptance of appointment signed by the appointed contractor. Option A confuses Form BA8 with Form BA10 (commencement notice) and cites an incorrect 48-hour timeline. Option C is wrong because Form BA14 is a completion certificate, not a cancellation instrument. Option D is incorrect as the statutory deadline is 7 days under Reg. 8(1), not 28 days.

questions.scenario: An RGBC holding a valid consent to commence superstructure works was forced to cease all site activities completely for 3.5 consecutive months due to an off-site legal dispute affecting site access. The dispute is settled on a Friday, and the client instructs the RGBC's Authorized Signatory to mobilize concrete trucks and recommence structural slab casting on Monday morning without further regulatory filings.
options: A. The RGBC can recommence immediately because the original consent issued under Section 16(1)(b) remains active until the final occupation permit is granted.

B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) because works ceased for more than 3 months; works cannot resume until an application for renewal of consent is submitted on Form BA9 under Section 20(2) and granted by the Building Authority.
C. The RGBC must only submit a fresh Form BA10 giving 7 days' advance notice of resumption to reactivate the original consent automatically without awaiting Building Authority approval.
D. The RGBC may recommence immediately provided an explanatory letter is submitted jointly by the RGBC and AP within 14 days of work resumption.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & (2); B(A)R Regulation 34; Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), a consent to commence building works is deemed to be revoked if the work is not commenced within 3 months of consent issuance, or if commenced, is stopped for more than 3 months. Since site works ceased for 3.5 months, the consent is legally revoked by operation of law. Under Section 20(2) and B(A)R Regulation 34, an application for renewal of consent must be made to the Building Authority on specified Form BA9 and formally granted before works can lawfully resume. Recommencing without renewed consent violates Section 14(1) and constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: The Building Authority issues formal consent to commence foundation works for a commercial development on Wednesday, 10 May. Eager to meet contractual milestones, the project director instructs the RGBC's Authorized Signatory to submit Form BA10 on Friday, 12 May, specifying Monday, 15 May as the commencement date, and to mobilize heavy drilling rigs to begin bored piling on that Monday.
options: A. The procedure is compliant because Form BA10 requires at least 48 hours of advance notice, excluding general holidays.
B. The procedure is unlawful because B(A)R Regulation 20(1) mandates that notice of commencement on Form BA10 must be given not less than 7 days before the specified commencement date.
C. The procedure is lawful because obtaining the written consent under Section 16(1)(b) automatically permits commencement on any date after consent issuance.
D. The procedure is acceptable provided the Authorized Person countersigns Form BA10 within 14 days after the rigs have commenced drilling.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1); Form BA10; BO Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1), an RGBC to whom consent has been given must give to the Building Authority not less than 7 days' notice of the date on which it is intended to commence the building works in the specified form (Form BA10). Submitting Form BA10 on 12 May specifying a commencement date of 15 May provides only 3 days' notice, directly contravening Regulation 20(1). Commencing works without fulfilling the statutory notice requirement constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A) of the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: A 40-storey mixed commercial and residential tower has attained practical physical completion. The developer intends to apply immediately for an Occupation Permit (OP) for the entire completed development under Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance. The project team must compile the mandatory statutory certificates and application forms for submission to the Building Authority.
options: A. The AP must submit Form BA13 accompanied by the RGBC's certificate on Form BA14A.
B. The AP must submit Form BA12 accompanied by the RGBC's certificate of completion of building works on Form BA14.
C. The RGBC must submit Form BA14 directly to the Building Authority, which automatically triggers the issuance of the OP within 14 days without AP involvement.
D. The AP and RGBC must jointly submit Form BA9 confirming practical completion under Section 21(6).
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 21; B(A)R Regulation 25(1); Forms BA12 & BA14
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 25(1) and Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance, when a whole new building has been completed, application for an Occupation Permit is made by the Authorized Person on specified Form BA12 ('Application for occupation permit in respect of a new building'). This application must be accompanied by the Registered General Building Contractor's completion certificate on specified Form BA14 ('Certificate of completion of building works'). Form BA13 is used for a Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) or partial OP under Section 21(2). Form BA14A is used by Registered Specialist Contractors, and Form BA9 is for renewal of consent.

questions.scenario: On a large commercial complex project, specialized mechanical ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems as well as fire service installations were executed under separate specialist consent by Registered Specialist Contractors (RSCs). Upon completion of all works, the main RGBC's Authorized Signatory signs Form BA14 purporting to certify both the general building envelope and all specialized installations to expedite the OP application.
options: A. The Building Authority will accept Form BA14 as comprehensive certification since an RGBC holds statutory umbrella authority over all specialist works on site.
B. Each Registered Specialist Contractor must execute and submit their own certificate of completion on specified Form BA14A under B(A)R Regulation 25(2) for their respective specialized categories.
C. An RGBC is legally forbidden from signing Form BA14 whenever any specialist contractor is present on site; only the Authorized Person can execute Form BA14.
D. Specialist works do not require any statutory completion certificate if the Fire Services Department has already issued a Form FSD 501.
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 25(2), where consent has been given in respect of a specialized category of building works (or where works are carried out by an RSC under a separate specialist consent), the Registered Specialist Contractor must execute and submit a certificate of completion on specified Form BA14A ('Certificate of completion of works by Registered Specialist Contractor'). An RGBC cannot usurp the statutory certification responsibilities of an RSC by signing Form BA14 for specialized works. Doing so violates B(A)R Regulation 25 and will invalidate the OP application.

questions.scenario: A building owner appoints an Authorized Person (AP) and an RGBC to carry out Class I Minor Works comprising the removal of an existing external reinforced concrete canopy projecting over a private lane. The AP prepares the prescribed plans. Under the Minor Works Control System (Cap. 123N), the contractor's Authorized Signatory must adhere to strict procedural submission timelines before commencing physical demolition.
options: A. The RGBC must submit Form MW03 accompanied by photos to the Building Authority within 14 days after completion of the works.
B. The AP and RGBC must submit the notice of commencement on specified Form MW01 together with prescribed plans to the Building Authority not less than 7 days before commencement.
C. The RGBC can commence immediately upon appointment and submit Form MW05 within 28 days of completing the works.
D. Because it is a demolition work involving structural concrete, the Simplified Requirements do not apply and a full Form BA10 under B(A)R Reg. 20 must be lodged.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 27 & 28; Specified Form MW01
questions.rationale: Under Sections 27 and 28 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), for Class I Minor Works, the appointed Prescribed Building Professional (PBP, e.g. AP) and Prescribed Registered Contractor (PRC, e.g. RGBC) must submit a notice of commencement on specified Form MW01, together with the prescribed plans, to the Building Authority not less than 7 days before the commencement of the works. Form MW03 applies to Class II works without a PBP; Form MW05 applies to Class III works. Canopy removal meeting Class I criteria falls squarely within Cap. 123N and does not require Form BA10.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is appointed directly by a commercial property manager to execute Class II Minor Works (Item 2.16 - erection of internal non-bearing block walls) where the statutory criteria under Cap. 123N Schedule 1 do not require the appointment of a Prescribed Building Professional (PBP). Following timely submission of Form MW03 and flawless execution of the works within 3 weeks, the RGBC must finalize the statutory filing upon completion.
options: A. The RGBC must submit a certificate of completion on specified Form MW06, together with photographic records of the works, within 14 days after completion of the works.
B. The RGBC must submit Form MW02 countersigned by an Authorized Person within 7 days after completion.
C. The RGBC is not required to submit any completion certificate because Class II works without a PBP are fully deemed approved upon expiry of the Form MW03 notice.
D. The RGBC must submit Form MW05 accompanied by as-built plans signed by a Registered Structural Engineer within 28 days after completion.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 32; Specified Form MW06
questions.rationale: Under Section 32 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), where Class II minor works are carried out without a Prescribed Building Professional (PBP), the Prescribed Registered Contractor (RGBC) must, within 14 days after the completion of the works, submit a certificate of completion on specified Form MW06 to the Building Authority, accompanied by photographs showing the physical condition of the site immediately before and after the works. Form MW02 is used when a PBP is appointed. Form MW05 is exclusively for Class III works. No works under Cap. 123N are 'deemed approved' without completing the statutory filing.

questions.scenario: A homeowner engages an RGBC to carry out Class III Minor Works involving the installation of an external drying rack projecting not more than 750 mm from the exterior wall (Item 3.1). The owner questions why the RGBC did not submit any notification to the Buildings Department prior to drilling into the wall on the first day of work.
options: A. The RGBC committed a serious offence under Section 40(2A) because all minor works, including Class III, require at least 7 days' prior notice on Form MW01.

B. Under the simplified requirements for Class III minor works under Cap. 123N Section 35, no prior notice of commencement is required; the RGBC must submit Form MW05 with before-and-after photos within 14 days after completion.
C. Prior notification is waived only if the RGBC obtains an express verbal waiver from the Buildings Department's Minor Works Unit prior to commencing site work.
D. The RGBC was required to submit Form MW03 at least 48 hours before commencement, followed by Form MW04 upon completion.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 35; Specified Form MW05
questions.rationale: Under Section 35 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), Class III minor works (small-scale household works) do not require prior notice of commencement to the Building Authority. The statutory requirement is post-construction certification: the Prescribed Registered Contractor (e.g., RGBC or Registered Minor Works Contractor) must, within 14 days after the completion of the works, submit a certificate of completion on specified Form MW05 together with photographs taken before and after the works to the Building Authority. Forms MW01 and MW03 are prior notices applicable only to Class I and Class II works respectively.

questions.scenario: During the execution of Class I Minor Works on a commercial podium, severe contractual disputes arise between the building owner and the appointed RGBC. The owner formally terminates the RGBC and appoints a replacement RGBC to complete the balance of the structural alterations. The Authorized Person (AP) must regularize the change of contractor with the Building Authority under the Minor Works Control System.
options: A. The AP and the incoming RGBC must submit a notice of change of prescribed registered contractor on specified Form MW04 within 7 days after the change.
B. The entire scheme must be cancelled by withdrawing the original Form MW01 and resubmitting a fresh Form MW01 giving a new 28-day notice period.
C. The incoming RGBC may simply complete the works under the original contractor's name and sign the final Form MW02 at project completion.
D. Form BA8 must be submitted to the Building Authority because change of registered contractor across all classes of work is governed exclusively by B(A)R Regulation 8.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 27A; Specified Form MW04
questions.rationale: Under Section 27A (and corresponding sections 30A/33A) of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), if there is a change of Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) or Prescribed Registered Contractor (PRC) during the course of minor works, notice of change must be delivered to the Building Authority in the specified form (Form MW04: 'Notice of Change of Prescribed Building Professional / Prescribed Registered Contractor') within 7 days after the change occurs. Form BA8 applies to building works carried out under formal approval and consent under the main Ordinance, not to the simplified MWCS regime.

questions.scenario: A retail tenant requests an RGBC to create a 3.5m-wide opening in a 250mm-thick internal load-bearing reinforced concrete shear wall inside a multi-storey shopping centre. The contractor's AS suggests submitting this under the Minor Works Control System using Form MW01 as Class I minor works to avoid the lengthy formal plan approval and consent process under Sections 14 and 16 of the Buildings Ordinance.
options: A. The proposal is acceptable provided the works are designed and supervised by an appointed RSE and completed within 60 days.

B. The proposal is unlawful because forming an opening in an internal load-bearing wall exceeding the statutory dimensional and structural limits of Schedule 1 of Cap. 123N falls outside the MWCS; proceeding under Form MW01 constitutes unauthorized building works under Section 14(1) punishable under Section 40(2A).
C. The proposal is compliant because any internal structural alteration inside a commercial building qualifies as Class I Minor Works under Item 1.1.
D. The proposal is lawful provided the RGBC submits Form MW01 and pays a double statutory vetting surcharge to the Buildings Department.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1) & Section 40(2A); Building (Minor Works) Regulation Schedule 1
questions.rationale: Under Schedule 1 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), minor works items involving openings in load-bearing walls are subject to strict, tight dimensional restrictions (e.g. Item 1.13 permits openings in load-bearing walls only up to specific restricted widths and requires that the wall is not a shear wall or transfer wall, typically limiting openings to not more than 1m or 1.2m width). A 3.5m-wide opening in a 250mm shear wall fundamentally exceeds the prescribed minor works parameters. Executing such major structural works under the MWCS simplified procedure bypassing Section 14(1) formal plan approval and consent constitutes carrying out unauthorized building works, rendering the contractor liable to criminal prosecution under Section 40(2A) (fine up to HK$400,000 and 2 years' imprisonment).

questions.scenario: During an unannounced audit by Buildings Department (BD) officers on a 28-storey commercial construction site, the RGBC's Authorized Signatory is unable to produce hard copies of the current approved structural framing plans and the Site Safety Supervision Plan. The site agent presents high-resolution digital PDF versions on an iPad, claiming that keeping paper plans is obsolete and that the approved physical copies are safely kept at the contractor's head office 5 km away.
options: A. The RGBC is fully compliant because digital electronic copies accessible via tablets satisfy the modern inspection requirements under BD Practice Notes.

B. The RGBC is in breach of statutory requirements because Building (Administration) Regulation 10 explicitly mandates that approved plans and supervisory documents must be kept continuously on site during the execution of works.
C. The RGBC is only required to keep the contractor's internal shop drawings on site, while approved plans can be retained off-site by the Registered Structural Engineer.
D. The RGBC complies provided a formal statutory declaration is signed by the Authorized Signatory confirming the digital versions are identical to approved drawings.
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 10, every registered contractor carrying out building works shall keep on the site of the works a copy of the approved plans and any supervision plan prepared in respect of the works, accessible to the Building Authority at all times during working hours. Failure to do so constitutes an offence under Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2B). Showing digital files or keeping physical copies off-site at a head office does not satisfy the strict mandatory requirement of Reg. 10.

questions.scenario: Six months after the issuance of an Occupation Permit for a residential tower, a commercial dispute arises between the developer and the RGBC. The developer instructs the RGBC to return or dispose of all concrete cube test certificates, steel reinforcement mill certificates, and Site Safety Supervision Plan logbooks to clear out the site storage. The RGBC shreds these records, believing that their retention duty ended once the Occupation Permit was granted.
options: A. The RGBC acted lawfully because statutory retention duties for quality and supervision records expire upon the formal issuance of the Occupation Permit under Section 21.

B. The RGBC committed a statutory breach because Building (Administration) Regulation 11 mandates that the contractor must retain all test records, supervisory logs, and execution records for at least 12 months after the issuance of the occupation permit or completion acknowledgment.
C. The RGBC is exempt from liability provided all digital laboratory results were previously uploaded to the Authorized Person's server.
D. The RGBC is required to retain records for only 90 days following completion of works, after which records become the exclusive responsibility of the Building Authority.
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 11 imposes a strict duty on the registered contractor to retain all records of tests, site supervision logs, and quality documentation for a period of not less than 12 months from the date of completion of the building works or the issuance of the occupation permit (or acknowledgment of Form BA14). Destroying these records at 6 months post-OP is a direct contravention of Reg. 11, attracting penal sanctions under Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: An RGBC receives formal consent from the Building Authority to commence superstructure works on 10 March. Under commercial pressure to meet milestone deadlines, the Authorized Signatory submits Form BA10 (Notice of Intention to Commence Building Works) to the Buildings Department on 12 March, declaring that structural steel erection will formally commence on site on 15 March.
options: A. The notice is valid because Form BA10 requires only 48 hours' prior notification under the Buildings Ordinance.
B. The notice is valid because works may commence immediately once formal written consent has been granted under Section 16.

C. The notice is invalid because Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) mandates that Form BA10 must be submitted to the Building Authority not less than 7 days prior to the commencement of works.
D. The notice is invalid because commencement notices must be submitted concurrently with the initial building plan application.
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1), the registered contractor must give not less than 7 days' prior notice in the specified form (Form BA10) to the Building Authority before commencing any building works for which consent has been given. Submitting Form BA10 on 12 March for a 15 March commencement provides only 3 days' notice, which breaches Reg. 20(1). Any commencement prior to the full 7-day statutory period is unlawful.

questions.scenario: An RGBC obtained consent under Section 16(1)(b) to construct a deep basement. Following completion of diaphragm walling, works were completely suspended for 14 consecutive weeks due to a contractual dispute between the employer and main contractor. Having resolved the dispute, the RGBC plans to immediately restart bulk excavation without notifying the Buildings Department, arguing that the original consent remains valid for the entire contract duration.
options: A. The RGBC can resume excavation immediately because consent granted under Section 16 never expires until the building is completed.

B. The consent has lapsed because under Buildings Ordinance Section 20(1), consent is deemed revoked if works are suspended for more than 3 months; the RGBC must apply for renewal using Form BA9 under Section 20(2) and B(A)R Regulation 34.
C. The RGBC needs only to submit an updated construction program to the Authorized Person without involving the Building Authority.
D. The RGBC must submit a brand new general building plan application under Section 14(1) because lapsed consents permanently void approved structural drawings.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance Section 20(1) & 20(2); Building (Administration) Regulation 34; Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Buildings Ordinance Section 20(1), a consent to commence building works is deemed to be revoked if the works are not commenced within 3 months, or if commenced, are suspended for a period exceeding 3 months (approximately 13 weeks). Because works were suspended for 14 weeks, the consent lapsed. Under BO Section 20(2) and Building (Administration) Regulation 34, the contractor and AP must apply to the Building Authority for renewal of consent using Form BA9 and obtain endorsement before resuming works. (Note: B(A)R Reg. 27 was repealed; Section 20 governs consent expiry).

questions.scenario: During the construction of a critical cantilevered transfer plate on the 4th floor of a mixed-use development, the RGBC's Authorized Signatory and the designated Technically Competent Persons (TCP T4 and T3) are absent from the site for two consecutive days to attend an overseas trade expo. Concrete pouring continues unabated under the sole direction of an uncertificated junior foreman.
options: A. The arrangement is acceptable because continuous supervision under the Buildings Ordinance is satisfied so long as a general foreman is physically present on site.

B. The RGBC has breached Building (Administration) Regulation 26 and Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5)(a) by failing to provide continuous, competent supervision by designated qualified personnel during structural works.
C. The contractor is fully shielded from liability if the Registered Structural Engineer's TCP T3 stream representative was present on site.
D. An Authorized Signatory is legally entitled to delegate statutory supervisory duties to any site personnel for up to 7 calendar days without BD notification.
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 26 requires every registered contractor to provide continuous supervision to all building works being executed. Furthermore, under BO Section 9(5)(a) and the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision, the RGBC must ensure that designated competent supervisory personnel (including specified TCP grades in accordance with the Site Safety Supervision Plan) actively carry out site safety supervision. Leaving critical structural works under an uncertificated junior foreman while designated TCPs are overseas breaches both Reg. 26 and Section 9(5)(a).

questions.scenario: To facilitate the delivery and unloading of heavy structural steel trusses across a busy public sidewalk, an RGBC erects a temporary hoarding and covered walkway fronting the site boundary. Due to spatial constraints from an existing road sign, the RGBC erects the covered walkway with a clear internal pedestrian width of 0.95 metres and an internal clear headroom of 2.20 metres.
options: A. The walkway dimensions are acceptable because temporary covered walkways need only provide at least 2.0 metres headroom and 0.9 metres width under the Summary Offences Ordinance.

B. The walkway breaches Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 4 and Building (Planning) Regulations, which mandate a minimum clear walking width of 1.1 metres and a minimum clear headroom of 2.5 metres.
C. The RGBC is fully compliant provided overhead netting and flashing warning lights are installed at both walkway entrances.
D. Temporary covered walkways are exempt from prescribed dimensional standards if erected for fewer than 30 consecutive calendar days.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 4 (Appendix A) & Building (Planning) Regulations Regulation 49
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 4 (Hoardings, Covered Walkways and Gantries) and Building (Planning) Regulations Regulation 49, covered walkways erected over or adjoining public footpaths must maintain minimum dimensional clearances to ensure public safety: the clear internal width of the walkway must not be less than 1.1 metres, and the clear headroom throughout must not be less than 2.5 metres above the pavement. A width of 0.95m and headroom of 2.20m directly contravene these statutory and practice standards.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is executing deep trench excavation and lateral support works within the Railway Protection Zone, located 25 metres from an active Mass Transit Railway (MTR) underground tunnel. During excavation, geotechnical instrumentation indicates that cumulative ground settlement has reached 21 mm, exceeding the standard statutory alert limit of 20 mm established in the approved monitoring schedule.
options: A. The RGBC may continue excavation works at full speed provided daily monitoring readings are emailed to the MTR Corporation within 48 hours.

B. In accordance with PNRC 14 (PNAP APP-24) and approved consent conditions, reaching the 20 mm alert/suspension trigger requires the immediate suspension of works, notification of the Building Authority and MTR Corporation, and implementation of agreed contingency measures.
C. The Authorized Signatory has the sole statutory authority to increase the movement threshold to 35 mm without consulting the Building Authority or MTR.
D. The settlement trigger applies exclusively to railway tracks and catenaries, meaning that settlement of surrounding subsoil does not require any work stoppage.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 14 (PNAP APP-24) & Buildings Ordinance Section 17(1)
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 14 / PNAP APP-24, works within the Railway Protection Zone are governed by stringent performance criteria, where the standard maximum allowable movement/settlement trigger is 20 mm unless otherwise agreed by the Building Authority and the MTR Corporation. When movement reaches this 20 mm threshold, works must be suspended immediately, immediate notifications must be made to the BA and MTR, and remedial/contingency plans must be deployed. Unilateral alteration of trigger values by the contractor is illegal.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is registered with only one Authorized Signatory (AS) endorsed on its register. In the middle of constructing a complex 35-storey superstructure, the sole AS abruptly resigns due to severe ill health and gives 24 hours' written notice. The Managing Director of the contracting firm, who is an experienced chartered builder but not an approved AS, instructs the site team to continue casting columns while recruiting a replacement AS.
options: A. Works may proceed for up to 60 days without an AS provided the Registered Structural Engineer issues weekly structural safety certificates.

B. Under PNRC 38 Section 4 and the Buildings Ordinance, when the sole AS ceases to act, the contractor ceases to be qualified to carry out works and all building operations must cease immediately until a new AS is approved by the Building Authority.
C. The Managing Director can immediately assume statutory responsibilities as acting AS by submitting a declaration to the Buildings Department within 14 days.
D. Works can continue uninterrupted as long as the Registered Contractor Stream TCP T5 remains on site full-time.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 38 Section 4 & Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5), 9(6)
questions.rationale: Under Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 38 and Buildings Ordinance Sections 9(5) and 9(6), a registered contractor can only operate and certify works through its approved Authorized Signatories. When the sole AS resigns, dies, or ceases to act, the contractor can no longer satisfy registration requirements or perform statutory duties. All building works must cease immediately. Works cannot resume until an application for an acceptable replacement AS has been interviewed, recommended by the Contractors Registration Committee, and approved by the Building Authority.

questions.scenario: During the construction of a podium transfer structure, the RGBC encounters congested rebar detailing. The site project manager decides to reconfigure the main tension reinforcement of primary transfer girders by replacing 40mm Grade 500B high-yield bars with clustered 32mm bars, and modifies the beam cross-sectional dimensions by 150mm. The RGBC proceeds without prior BD submission, claiming these qualify as 'minor amendments' to be submitted upon completion under PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52.
options: A. The RGBC acted lawfully because dimensional and rebar changes within 15% are classified as non-structural minor amendments under PNRC 52.

B. The changes violate Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1) and PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52 because structural alterations to primary load-bearing transfer elements significantly affect structural integrity and strictly require prior plan approval and formal consent before execution.
C. The changes are permissible provided the commercial testing laboratory certifies that the yield capacity of the replaced bars is identical.
D. The contractor is permitted to self-certify structural alterations on transfer structures under the Minor Works Control System (Cap. 123N).
questions.statutoryRef: PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52 & Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1), Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under PNAP APP-55 and PNRC 52, the streamlined procedure for minor amendments applies strictly to non-fundamental adjustments that do not compromise structural stability, life safety, or statutory planning parameters. Alterations to primary structural transfer girders, including resizing cross-sections and reconfiguring primary flexural reinforcement, fundamentally affect structural integrity. Carrying out such works without prior formal plan submission, approval, and consent under BO Section 14(1) is a criminal offence under Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: On a complex deep excavation and foundation project, the RGBC appoints an experienced registered structural engineer employed by its joint venture engineering parent company to act concurrently as both the RGBC's Contractor Stream TCP T4 and the Registered Structural Engineer's (RSE) Stream TCP T4, aiming to enhance communication and streamline safety audits.
options: A. This concurrent appointment is strictly prohibited under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision because TCPs in the Contractor stream cannot be concurrently appointed in the AP/RSE stream to avoid conflict of interest and preserve independent supervision.
B. This concurrent appointment is fully permitted provided the engineer holds dual corporate memberships in ICE and HKIE.
C. The appointment is permissible only if approved in writing by the Authorized Person 3 days before work starts.
D. Concurrent appointment across streams is allowed for foundation works, but strictly prohibited for superstructure works above 30 metres.
questions.statutoryRef: Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) Section 5 & PNRC 38
questions.rationale: The Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) explicitly establishes distinct, independent supervisory streams: the AP/RSE/RGE stream (checking and verification stream) and the Contractor stream (executive and direct supervisory stream). The SSPS Code strictly prohibits any person from holding concurrent appointments across different streams (e.g., serving as both RSE TCP and Contractor TCP). Such cross-stream dual roles compromise independent oversight and invalidate the Site Safety Supervision Plan.
